“Description of the System” throughout the period June 1, 2024 to May 31, 2025 (description) based
on the criteria for a description of a service organization’s system set forth in DC 200, 2018 Description
Criteria for a Description of a Service Organization’s System in a SOC 2® Report (With Revised
Implementation Guidance—2022) (AICPA, Description Criteria), (description criteria) and the suitability
of the design and operating effectiveness of controls stated in the description throughout the period
June 1, 2024 to May 31, 2025, to provide reasonable assurance that Sequoia’s service commitments
and system requirements were achieved based on the trust services criteria relevant to security,
availability and confidentiality (applicable trust services criteria) set forth in TSP 100, 2017 Trust
Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (With Revised
Point of Focus—2022) (AICPA, Trust Services Criteria) and the implementation requirements set forth
in the HITRUST CSF version 9.6 that are applicable to Sequoia’s system required for a HITRUST CSF

Sequoia uses three subservice organizations, Amazon Web Services (“AWS”) to perform server
hosting, physical and environmental protection, network management, access authentication,
infrastructure management and disk storage, along with Salesforce (“SFDC”) and PrismHR to perform
aspects of computer processing for the cloud hosted applications that comprise the Sequoia People
Platform. The description indicates that complementary subservice organization controls that are
suitably designed and operating effectively are necessary, along with controls at Sequoia, to achieve
Sequoia’s service commitments and system requirements based on the applicable trust services
criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria. The description presents Sequoia’s controls, the applicable trust
services criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria, and the types of complementary subservice organization
controls assumed in the design of Sequoia’s controls. The description does not disclose the actual
controls at the subservice organization. Our examination did not include the services provided by the
subservice organization, and we have not evaluated the suitability of the design or operating
effectiveness of such complementary subservice organization controls.

M

Service Organization’s Responsibilities
Sequoia is responsible for its service commitments and system requirements and for designing,
implementing, and operating effective controls within the system to provide reasonable assurance
that Sequoia’s service commitments and system requirements were achieved.
In Section II, Sequoia has provided the accompanying assertion titled “Management’s Assertion”
(assertion) about the description and the suitability of design and operating effectiveness of controls
stated therein. Sequoia is also responsible for preparing the description and assertion, including the
completeness, accuracy, and method of presentation of the description and assertion; providing the
services covered by the description; selecting the applicable trust services criteria and HITRUST CSF
criteria and stating the related controls in the description; and identifying the risks that threaten the
achievement of the service organization’s service commitments and system requirements.

Service Auditor’s Responsibilities

1:1
6.3
70

Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the description and on the suitability of design and
operating effectiveness of controls stated in the description based on our examination. Our
examination was conducted in accordance with attestation standards established by the American
Institute of Certified Public Accountants. Those standards require that we plan and perform our
examination to obtain reasonable assurance about whether, in all material respects, the description is
presented in accordance with the description criteria and that the controls stated therein were suitably
designed and operated effectively to provide reasonable assurance that the service organization's
service commitments and system requirements were achieved based on the applicable trust services
criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria. We believe that the evidence we obtained is sufficient and
appropriate to provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.
An examination of a description of a service organization’s system and the suitability of the design
and operating effectiveness of controls involves—
Obtaining an understanding of the system and the service organization's service
commitments and system requirements.

•

Assessing the risks that the description is not presented in accordance with the description
criteria and that controls were not suitably designed or did not operate effectively.

•

Performing procedures to obtain evidence about whether the description is presented in
accordance with the description criteria.

•

Performing procedures to obtain evidence about whether controls stated in the description
were suitably designed to provide reasonable assurance that the service organization
achieved its service commitments and system requirements based on the applicable trust
services criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria.

•

Testing the operating effectiveness of controls stated in the description to provide reasonable
assurance that the service organization achieved its service commitments and system
requirements based on the applicable trust services criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria.

•

Evaluating the overall presentation of the description.

The description is prepared to meet the common needs of a broad range of report users and may not,
therefore, include every aspect of the system that individual report users may consider important to
meet their informational needs. There are inherent limitations in any system of internal control,
including the possibility of human error and the circumvention of controls.

M

Because of their nature, controls may not always operate effectively to provide reasonable assurance
that the service organization’s service commitments and system requirements are achieved based on
the applicable trust services criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria. Also, the projection to the future of any
conclusions about the suitability of the design or operating effectiveness of controls is subject to the
risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions or that the degree of
compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.

Sequoia Group and Sequoia One PEO, LLC (“Sequoia” or “the Company”) help businesses get their
total people investment right, so they have the team they need to win. With Sequoia’s expert consulting
and powerful platform for benefits, compensation, and overall people programs, global employers of
all sizes can drive measurable outcomes and employee engagement through their total rewards
strategy. Sequoia has spent 24 years supporting the world’s most innovative, market-changing
companies and knows what it takes to fuel a business’s growth and please their people. Sequoia has
offices in San Mateo, CA, New York, NY, Tempe, AZ, Irvine, CA, Rochester, NY, Mexico City, Mexico,
and Bangalore, India.

The Sequoia People Platform

pla

ne

o,

20

25

While HR teams manage the most influential assets of a company, its employees, very few companies
consider HR as a full partner in developing and implementing the business strategy. HR can become
a full partner in implementing the business strategy by demonstrating talent management benefits
and bottom-line impact. To show the impact, HR should first concentrate on an integrated employee
management approach. The current market HCM/HRIS solution enables an approach for integrated
employee management. While closed ecosystems offer better control, they limit the choice for
companies to pick and choose.

ike
g@

Sequoia's approach is an integrated, digital experience that allows HR to keep existing technologies
or adopt new ones. Sequoia brings guidance to create the marketplace for world-class solutions for
integrated employee management.

Gu
ze
w

icz

,m

Connectivity is key. HR departments can keep the tools and systems they love and integrate them to
share and surface information with the company. By connecting systems, HR departments can not
only create the integrated, digital experience employees demand, but also gain access to the data and
information needed to properly track and analyze human capital.

M

ike

Consider the strategic value of being able to accurately see in real-time the true value - including
historical data, recruiting, benefits, training, employee development and engagement and retention of each employee. Getting access to this data means cobbling together reports from disparate tools
that quickly become obsolete without connectivity. HR professionals cannot evaluate the whole
employee picture needed to make strategic decisions.
Sequoia collects employer-provided/linked data to provide the platform with capabilities that enable
management of people, compensation, and benefits programs. Clients of Sequoia can plan, analyze
and execute on their people investment data. The Total Rewards Advisory (TRA) platform includes
benefits, compensation, and equity information.

Sequoia’s outsourced HR offering is a multi-function, orchestrated service offering. In order to deliver
and scale the service, Sequoia utilizes cloud-based services such as Microsoft Office 365, Amazon
Web Services (AWS) and multiple Salesforce products (including centralized knowledge sharing,
unified client data, case management, and dashboards) to coordinate service delivery execution and
management.

Sequoia’s leadership understands that by providing outsourced HR services, clients entrust Sequoia
with confidential and private information. This responsibility is one Sequoia’s leadership takes
seriously. Leadership has increased year-over-year investment in tools, processes, and personnel to
improve and modernize internal controls over client’s confidential and private data. Leadership utilizes
dedicated time in company all hands meetings, as well as periodic communications from IT security,
legal and other department heads, to communicate and reinforce Sequoia’s security practices,
policies, and internal controls.

When joining the Company, each Sequoia team member reviews and acknowledges receipt and

A critical part of ensuring a work environment with strong ethics and controls starts with the hiring
and training process. The Sequoia people team manages a consistent process for sourcing and
assessing candidates, including screening applicants, ensuring background checks are completed,
and orientation of new team members. All new team members go through orientation classes that
introduce them to the Company culture, business, policies, and various departments within the
Company.

Section III – Description of the System
Control Environment (continued)
Background Checks
Sequoia performs background checks on all team members, and documented job descriptions exist
for each position in the Company. As part of Sequoia's commitment to competence, all team members
are required to participate in formal bi-annual review meetings, where their performance is evaluated,
and team members are coached to meet or exceed Sequoia standards by their managers.

New Hire Onboarding

-10

-16

T2
0:5

1:1
6.3
70
Z

Before an individual joins Sequoia, management must first identify the need for additional personnel.
A job requisition and job description are drafted and approved by the appropriate manager and by the
people team. Once the requisition has been completed, a job description is drafted. The talent
acquisition (TA) team sources candidates and reviews resumes to identify qualified candidates, and
once the candidate is identified, they are further evaluated through a phone screening process. If the
candidate passes the phone screening, they are scheduled for a combination of virtual and onsite in
person interviews with the individuals on the interview panel, consisting of the direct team, leadership,
and cross-functional interviewers. When interviews are completed, a hiring decision is made and
potentially, an offer letter is issued. If the prospective employee formally accepts the offer letter, the
TA team completes a background check. The formal background check and hiring steps must be
completed before the prospective employee is allowed access to begin work.

ne
ra.
i

o,

20

25

The new employee completes the new hire orientation and is required to provide written
acknowledgement of the team member handbook and the acceptable use policy. The new employee
may also complete HIPAA training depending on their role, as well as additional training necessary to
fulfill their role at Sequoia. Training continues throughout the year on diverse topics including
information security and privacy.

Policy for Training

icz

Performance Management

,m

ike
g@

pla

New team members receive an orientation meeting to introduce general Sequoia procedures, as well
as position-specific training from managers or more experienced team members as they assume their
job responsibilities. Sequoia team members are trained in the risks of teleworking and mobile
computing and bring your own device usage. Sequoia provides team member training on various
security topics that are reasonable and appropriate.

M

ike

Gu
ze
w

The overall approach to performance management is through a series of ongoing conversations,
resources, learning programs and tools to help managers and team members work effectively
together. In addition to the bi-annual reviews, the output of the ongoing performance management
process for each employee includes a goal plan, a development plan, and a summary of key
conversations throughout the year. Goal planning includes a discussion of expectations around
results, priorities, and core job responsibilities. The development plan and key conversations focus on
defining and planning for areas of growth in the employee's current roles tied to the Company's
strategy, areas of strength and improvement, and address risks that may impact the Company or
within their areas of responsibilities.

Employment Termination
Employment can be terminated by Sequoia at any time as it operates as an at-will employer. Employee
terminations can be voluntary or involuntary.

Section III – Description of the System
Risk Assessment & Management
Business and Information Security Risk Management
Sequoia’s leadership understands the importance of protecting the Company’s information systems
and data, which includes its clients’ data. Therefore, Sequoia has invested and continues to invest in
security and data protection across people, processes, and technology. Sequoia’s C-team, including
the chief information security officer, and leadership team oversee and address cybersecurity risk and
has appointed the VP of global security to develop and implement the necessary policies, processes,
and procedures to manage and monitor the Company’s cybersecurity risk.

T2
0:5

1:1
6.3

Sequoia’s C-team, including the chief information security officer, and leadership team are responsible

facilitate Sequoia’s information security compliance efforts and security program and make
recommendations to improve Sequoia’s information security posture and to ensure compliance with
applicable laws and regulations. These teams are responsible for identifying and assessing the related
risks and implementing appropriate risk management practices. The teams review, advise, and direct
management with respect to strategic business risks, operational risks, legal risks, and regulatory
risks, among others.

Sequoia undergoes periodic internal and external (third party) risk assessments to identify areas

IT and security follows a risk-based approach to focus on securing critical information systems and
data. IT and security assesses the security controls in place as well as their maturity and potential
threats that would compromise the integrity of the security controls. Areas of improvement are
identified, and remediation initiatives and activities are prioritized to address potential areas of risk.
Security controls are continuously monitored to ensure their integrity and robustness. The
cybersecurity risk management cycle continues with identification, classification, and assessment of
controls again, using a cyclical method to ensure that the system works, and risks are identified and
addressed.

Monitoring Activities

M

ike

Gu
ze
w

icz

Sequoia’s managers and leadership reviews daily, weekly, and monthly reports detailing metrics for
processing and quality. These reports help management stay on top of the status of the business and
to identify when controls may not be functioning as designed. Company team members are also
encouraged and empowered to surface concerns or suggestions that can improve processes or
reduce risk. Company management and executives also stay abreast of industry trends and risks
through their active involvement in industry trade organizations. The Company also uses logging and
monitoring software such as Salesforce, SentinelOne, Cisco Umbrella, CloudWatch, CloudTrail,
Datadog, DataSunrise, a mobile device management (MDM) solution and a security information and
event management (SIEM) solution to collect data from system infrastructure components and from
endpoint systems and to monitor and secure those systems. The logging and monitoring software is
used to monitor system performance, potential security threats and vulnerabilities, and resource
utilization, and to detect unusual system activity or service requests. The software sends alert
messages to the appropriate team members when security events are detected. The identified
deficiencies and events are communicated to the necessary personnel and appropriate corrective
actions are initiated.

Policies and Procedures
Policies and procedures are a key tool for process standardization and communication of key control
elements. Each newly hired Sequoia team member is trained in security and reviews and
acknowledges receipt and understanding of the acceptable use policy when they join the Company.
All team members are trained in security annually. The purpose of the acceptable use policy is to
protect Sequoia’s information systems and company data by:
Establishing appropriate information security and system practices when using and/or
accessing company information systems and company data.

•

Informing individuals of their responsibilities for using and/or accessing company information
systems and company data.

•

Ensuring compliance with company policies, applicable laws and regulations regarding the
use and/or access of company information systems and company data.

The information security policy sets the direction and demonstrates the commitment of the Company
to information security and the protection of company information systems and data, including client
data. The policy and related processes and procedures describe the steps needed to perform certain
tasks or to carry out security responsibilities. They identify the personnel or teams to whom they apply,
and they ensure consistency in implementation and operations. The policy and related processes and
procedures are updated periodically, as needed, and as the business, regulatory environment, and risk
considerations change. The policy is authorized by Sequoia’s C-team, and it is supported at the highest
levels of Sequoia’s leadership, including the chief information security officer. Sequoia’s VP of global
security is responsible for implementing and maintaining the information security policy, as well as
providing guidance and advice on its implementation to Sequoia’s C-team and leadership team.

Network Security Overview
Sequoia has a minimal IT infrastructure footprint and leverages the AWS computing platform to build
and run technological solutions to support its core services. In addition, Sequoia’s IT operating model
partners with world-class solutions and service providers to deliver services, thus minimizing reliance
and operational overhead related to hosting and managing traditional infrastructure. IT operations and
security controls administration are shared with AWS and third-party solutions and service providers
to deliver an operationally efficient and secure cloud computing environment.

1:1
6.3
70
Z

Sequoia leverages third party cloud solutions, platforms, and data centers to provide services to its
clients. The third parties enter into agreements with Sequoia that cover their privacy and security
responsibilities. Sequoia utilizes AWS for certain core computing and storage needs. The AWS hosting
platform implements strong security and privacy controls and offers the following accreditations and
certifications to demonstrate its commitment to privacy and security: SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2,
SOC 3, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, CSA, PCI DSS Level 1, and others.

20

25

-10

-16

T2
0:5

Sequoia’s backend infrastructure resides in a dedicated, secure AWS environment that uses Amazon
Elastic Container Service (ECS), Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3), Amazon’s Elastic Compute
Cloud (EC2), Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS), Amazon Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) and
Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) that are designed with fault tolerance and
high availability in mind using Amazon’s availability zones model. Physical and environmental security
is provided via the AWS hosted platform. Sequoia utilizes Imperva’s web application firewall (WAF) as
well as Amazon’s firewalls to limit network access to only the necessary services allowed for
Sequoia’s AWS-hosted services to function. In addition, the production environment is logically
separate and non-accessible from non-production environments.

o,

Sequoia uses AWS and Salesforce for its core server hosting and technology platforms. The data
centers are physically secured with environmental controls in place, and they are staffed with security
personnel 24/7. The service providers and their data centers undergo independent SOC 1 and SOC 2
audits and maintain multiple compliance and security certifications and attestations.

,m

ike
g@

All sensitive data transmitted is encrypted to protect against third-party disclosure in transit. Servers
and network components are secured with access control mechanisms and protected by industry
standard firewalls and intrusion detection systems (IDS). All security services are monitored and
updated based on their risk profile to address emerging vulnerabilities. The corporate Sequoia network
is also protected by DNS-based security filtering.

icz

Remote Access

Wireless Security

M

ike

Gu
ze
w

All remote access to Sequoia information systems is via approved secure protocols such as SSL/TLS,
virtual private network (VPN) and secure shell (SSH). These protocols allow systems to establish and
maintain trusted connections for information exchange. Remote connections enabling data exchange
without encryption in-transit are prohibited. Core systems are cloud-based and accessed via Azure
single sign on (SSO) with Island Enterprise Browser and multi-factor authentication (MFA) required.
Two separate wireless networks are used at each office location, a guest and a corporate Sequoia
network. The two wireless networks are separated and traffic from one network cannot reach the
other. The WPA2 enterprise security protocol is used for securing and encrypting wireless
communications after user authentication. All wireless access points are installed in physically secure
locations and tracked by IT and security.

16
Sequoia Proprietary and Confidential – Redistribution Prohibited

Section III – Description of the System
Network Security Overview (continued)
Antivirus and Firewalls
Team members are assigned laptops for business purposes. Any unauthorized software that has not
been approved by the Company is not permitted to be installed on those systems. Furthermore,
Sequoia controls the introduction of new software into the environment by restricting the ability to
install software on endpoints and laptops to team members. Only authorized IT team members can
install software and any exceptions are managed. External storage devices are restricted from
connecting to machines, further minimizing the possibility of malicious software from executing or
installing on Sequoia systems.

1:1
6.3
70
Z

Antivirus and antimalware software are installed on all endpoints. Sequoia uses a next-gen endpoint
detection and response (EDR) solution to protect endpoints. If a security event triggers the solution
on any machine, IT support and security receive an alert via the ticketing system and investigate.

-10

-16

T2
0:5

SentinelOne is deployed to Sequoia endpoints. SentinelOne is a fully managed endpoint detection and
response (MDR) solution that provides 24x7x365 monitoring and incident response assistance. For
known threats, it provides cloud-based antivirus and indicators of compromise (IOC) detection
capabilities. For unknown and zero-day threats, it applies indicators of attack (IOA) detection
capabilities, using machine learning techniques to build predictive models that can detect neverbefore-seen malicious activities with high accuracy. This IOA analysis recognizes behavioral patterns
to detect new attacks, whether they use malware or not.

pla

ne
ra.
i

o,

20

25

Sequoia utilizes firewalls and lines of defense in AWS such as security groups and network ACLs for
controlling inbound and outbound traffic and for protecting internal systems, as well as IDS to thwart
unusual or unauthorized activity. Network traffic is inspected and managed to prevent internal
systems and applications to directly connect and communicate with untrusted systems. Default deny
rules are configured so that only essential network protocols, ports and services are allowed to
connect to the Sequoia network and systems. External access to sensitive data is restricted by user
authentication and message encryption systems including VPN, SSH and TLS.

ike
g@

In addition, a DNS-based security filtering solution protects systems from undesired outbound
connections and communications.

,m

Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing

ike

Gu
ze
w

icz

An automated scanning solution is used to scan all Sequoia infrastructure such as servers and
network devices. Vulnerabilities are reviewed, assessed, and prioritized for remediation based on their
severity and risk they pose to the business. In addition, both internal and external penetration tests
are conducted by an independent third party and identified vulnerabilities are reported with prioritized
remediation recommendations. Management ranks all identified vulnerabilities for remediation and
develops mitigation strategies to address identified vulnerabilities in a timely manner.

M

User Accounts, Access and Reviews
User accounts are created for authorized team members to be able to access the systems they need
for performing their job responsibilities. Permissions are then assigned following a role-based access
control (RBAC) approach so that users are only able to perform their jobs. Accounts are reviewed
periodically to ensure access is assigned to authorized team members. Unnecessary accounts that
are identified are immediately disabled or appropriate actions is taken for remediation.
Administrator access is restricted to the appropriate system administrators based on their job
responsibilities. For core systems, security and IT performs a periodic administrator account review
to ensure access is assigned to the appropriate team members that have administration
authorization.

17
Sequoia Proprietary and Confidential – Redistribution Prohibited

Section III – Description of the System
Network Security Overview (continued)
User Accounts, Access and Reviews (continued)
Access controls for Sequoia domain-linked systems are managed via security groups and
membership to those groups requires management approval. A centralized solution is used to allow
users to easily and securely access the information systems they need to perform their job
responsibilities.

1:1
6.3
70
Z

Sensitive Sequoia data is protected using a layering of controls, including access controls, to ensure
that it is not improperly disclosed, modified, deleted, or rendered unavailable. All access is granted
using the least privilege principle if there is a business need and only with manager approval. Formal
procedures exist for user access, from the initial registration of new users to the final de-registration
of users who no longer require access to information systems and services.

Passwords are confidential Sequoia data and must be closely protected. The following guidelines
apply to the confidentiality of Sequoia’s passwords:
Team members must not disclose or share their passwords with anyone (co-workers,
supervisors, family, etc.).

•

Team members must not write down their passwords or leave them unsecured.

•

Team members must not use the same password for different systems and/or accounts.

•

Team members must not send passwords via email.

•

Team members must not re-use passwords even if the application or system allows them to.

System Passwords (continued)
In addition to entering the username and password and before accessing Azure B2C-integrated
applications, a second authentication factor is also required such as a code sent to the team
member’s mobile phone. Only after the correct credentials and the correct code are entered can the
team member access the application. This authentication mechanism greatly improves security and
prevents attacks on the application.

For production systems, new servers and containers are periodically deployed to support business

restricted only to authorized personnel. Before such a server is deployed, it must be assigned the
appropriate access and/or AWS network ACL(s) and security group(s), as applicable, to prevent
unauthorized access and malicious attacks. Default or vendor-supplied credentials and settings are
changed and unneeded accounts on the systems are disabled.

Outage Notifications
Outage notifications and incidents are updated at https://status.sequoia.com. The status page will be
updated for any incident that impacts Sequoia’s systems with regular notifications on progress being
made on the incidents. Normally maintenance windows do not impact clients as the Sequoia People
Platform is highly available even while changes/updates are being made. If any maintenance or
change impacts the Sequoia People Platform, the status page is updated promptly.

Security & Incident Management

-10

-16

T2
0:5

1:1
6.3
70
Z

A cybersecurity incident is defined as a single or series of unwanted or unexpected information
security events that have a significant probability of impacting the confidentiality, integrity, and
availability of information systems and/or Sequoia data. Not all cybersecurity events are incidents. A
cybersecurity event is an identified occurrence(s) of a system, service, or network state indicating a
possible violation of information security policy, technology control failure, or a previously unknown
situation that may be security relevant. To handle cybersecurity events and incidents, a robust security
and incident management capability has been implemented which includes a cybersecurity incident
response plan, triggered when a reported or detected data incident has occurred or is believed to have
occurred. The plan defines the responsibilities of Sequoia team members involved in the incident and
provides guidelines for responding efficiently and effectively.

25

This plan is intended to ensure that Sequoia is prepared if an incident were to occur and provides
guidance if an incident is suspected, covering both electronic and physical security.

ne
ra.
i

o,

20

All incidents are logged and acted upon, and the procedure is reviewed and updated periodically, as
needed. Communications are a key component of incident response and occur throughout the
incident lifecycle. The core phases of the incident management (adapted from SANS Institute and
NIST model) are as follows:

Application Security

M

ike

The core applications comprising the Sequoia People Platform and that are used to provide Sequoia’s
services to Sequoia’s clients, are third party hosted and/or deployed via a SaaS-based model. Vendors
and service providers that Sequoia partners with and that support or provide services to Sequoia, also
sign a subcontractor BAA as required, which covers their responsibilities and obligations when it
comes to protecting Sequoia and client information.
Core system applications for the Sequoia People Platform such as AWS and Salesforce are accessed
via Entra using MFA. This authentication mechanism greatly improves security as it requires users to
authenticate using their account and password as well as a code that they receive (second
authentication factor) to access the applications. All mobile application and web application code, for
users accessing benefits data and services, is developed using secure development practices, tested
using both automated tools as well as manual testing, and updated regularly to ensure the Sequoia
mobile application and Admin web application remain up to date.

System Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
Sequoia assembles its Sequoia People Platform from a combination of COTS and custom-developed
software. COTS software implementations follow a standard process of requirements gathering,
analysis and design, build, test and deploy. Sequoia utilizes internal resources for creative design
(UI/UX), iOS and Android mobile application development, Admin web application development, QA
and project management services. For custom-developed software, a slightly different methodology
is followed as described below.

T2
0:5

1:1
6.3
70
Z

The engineering group is responsible for all maintenance of existing Sequoia-built software
applications, tailoring existing applications and development of new applications. The IT request (ITR)
lifecycle begins with the business requirements analysis and ends with the user acceptance testing
(UAT) process which follows the general iterative principle of analysis, design, development and
review. The ITR documentation consists of the following items which are tracked in Jira tickets:
request, functional specifications, project impact analysis, project plan, test script, developer release
notes, code review signoff, IT testing (ITT), UAT signoff, and implementation notes.

25

-10

-16

The engineering group follows general coding rules, including naming conventions and project setup
and architecture, including the required use of a code repository. A code review is performed in the
development environment by a senior code reviewer. The engineering group then approves the
changes and transfers approved programs from engineering to quality engineering for testing and
verification prior to moving to production.

ne
ra.
i

o,

20

Atlassian Jira is an agile project management tool that tracks status, estimated vs. actual time to
completion in all project phases, assignment of project-specific tasks and sub-tasks, bug tracking and
reporting. Jira is comprised of these main items:
Product - an application or system currently in production. Work orders can be assigned to
products for basic IT requests. Tickets are used to log production bugs.

•

Project - new development or involved IT request. Work orders are assigned to projects or subprojects by functional area. Tickets are used to log development bugs.

•

Tickets - used to track a programming issue or problem generally referred to as a "bug".
Production bugs are attached to products and development bugs are attached to projects.

Change Management Policy
Change management is critical in ensuring that changes to Sequoia systems such as application
servers, databases and network devices are managed properly to optimize business services and
processes that depend on such resources and to minimize the impact and service interruption that
may occur from these changes.

22
Sequoia Proprietary and Confidential – Redistribution Prohibited

Section III – Description of the System
Network Security Overview (continued)
Change Management Policy (continued)
The change management policy was enacted to control and monitor changes to Sequoia platform.
Change control is also applied to Sequoia-developed applications and Salesforce platforms and
applications. Workflows for changes are thoroughly documented and tested, as appropriate, and
require multi-step approval. Project management and ticketing system Jira is used to track and
monitor the status and ownership of all infrastructure, systems, and Sequoia-developed application
changes. Because each request is stored as an electronic ticket, the speed of the approval process is
significantly increased and reduces the need for additional meetings to review and approve requests.

Additional Controls Related to Availability

-16

T2
0:5

Sequoia has a variety of monitoring tools within AWS, where its digital products are hosted, and
outside of AWS. Inside AWS, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and Security Hub are used. Outside
of AWS, Datadog is used to monitor systems’ availability, performance, and security vulnerabilities to
trigger alerts and notifications when certain thresholds are breached. For security incident monitoring
and response, we also use a variety of monitoring and alerting solutions external to AWS including
Sumo Logic (SIEM), Cisco Umbrella, SentinelOne and Netskope.

-10

Sequoia’s core technology platform is fully cloud-based. Sequoia backs up the data periodically and
the data is encrypted when it is transmitted, and it is also encrypted while stored within the cloudbased platform or offsite using a third-party service.

ne
ra.
i

o,

Office 365 data is stored in Microsoft’s cloud infrastructure, with built-in data redundancy and
encryption. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256, and data in transit is encrypted using TLS. Each
application backup is encrypted using a separate key, following envelope encryption practices, which
ensures that the compromise of one key does not affect the security of other backups.

Gu
ze
w

icz

,m

ike
g@

pla

As of July 30, 2023, Sequoia fully transitioned to a cloud-based infrastructure and no longer utilizes
on-premises systems. Azure Backup is now used to protect cloud-based resources, including virtual
machines, Azure Files, and other supported workloads. Backup jobs are scheduled according to the
criticality of the systems, with daily backups for critical services and less frequent schedules for noncritical resources. Azure Backup supports incremental backups, reducing storage and bandwidth
usage while maintaining the ability to perform point-in-time restores. All backup data is encrypted in
transit using TLS and at rest using AES-256 encryption. Azure employs per-item encryption and key
management to ensure that each backup is protected with unique encryption keys, enhancing data
isolation and security. Data is stored redundantly across Azure regions, providing resiliency and
ensuring recoverability in the event of a failure or disaster.

M

ike

Management reviews backup reports for cloud-hosted applications to determine that proper data
backup controls are in place and operating effectively.
In AWS, automated backup routines are in place to create snapshot images of critical EC2 instance
volumes daily. These instance snapshots are stored in the highly redundant Amazon S3. In AWS, data
is stored in AWS RDS and in MongoDB. All data is backed up automatically daily. Transaction failures
for RDS and MongoDB instances generate an alert, and the DevOps team takes action to resolve any
issues. Critical S3 buckets are replicated across two AWS regions for redundancy and disaster
recovery. All backups are encrypted both in transit and at rest.

Section III – Description of the System
Additional Controls Related to Availability (continued)
Disaster Recovery

1:1
6.3
70
Z

Planning for the business continuity of Sequoia in the aftermath of a disaster is an essential part of
an organization’s risk management program. Preparation for, response to, and recovery from a
disaster affecting the administrative functions of the Company require the cooperative efforts of many
functional areas and supporting organizations. Because Sequoia’s infrastructure is mainly cloudhosted via AWS, Salesforce and other SaaS platforms, a disaster event occurring at the Company’s
headquarters would not significantly impact production systems or services. Team members would
be able to work from other locations and if there is Internet access, they would be able to access the
systems they need to support operations and services.

T2
0:5

Sequoia maintains a business continuity plan (BCP) to address the risks related to a disaster affecting
people, facilities, and technology. In addition, there are separate disaster recovery plans for core IT
infrastructure components taking into consideration the operations necessary to restore services to
remote locations if there is a disaster at Sequoia’s headquarters or at the third-party hosting locations
that would impact the Company and/or its operations.

-16

Sequoia performs business continuity and disaster recovery tests for the following critical business
applications.

Additional Controls Related to Confidentiality
Data Retention
Sequoia provides a multitude of healthcare-related and HR benefit services, including services as a
covered entity under HIPAA. Accordingly, Sequoia is required to retain data to comply with HIPAA and
other state and federal healthcare data retention requirements. Sequoia retains copies of PHI to
provide services to its clients and retains that data for the period required to comply with applicable
state and federal laws. Sequoia deletes PHI upon client or individual request to comply with state and
federal data privacy laws, unless required to retain that data under applicable law.

Section III – Description of the System
Complementary Subservice Organization Controls
Subservice Organization Controls
Sequoia utilizes subservice organizations to perform the functions described below to improve
operating and administrative effectiveness. Third party personnel are not granted access to Sequoia
or user entity data or the Sequoia systems themselves. The examination by the Independent Service
Auditor did not extend to the policies and procedures at these subservice organizations.

T2
0:5

1:1
6.3
70
Z

Sequoia relies on AWS for data center and infrastructure hosting. AWS is designed with fault tolerance
protection for all layers of the platform and infrastructure, including routers, switches, load balancers
and firewalls, as well as web and application services and backend database connections. The cloud
infrastructure is designed to accommodate foreseeable growth in the number of participants and
transaction volume for their on-demand products and services. Sequoia monitors the performance of
these activities with the monitoring tools described above. Issues or relevant exceptions are
investigated further for impact to Sequoia’s applications. In the event of a disaster, Sequoia can run
the business from an existing alternative data center location, utilizing the data backup located within
the AWS network.

20

25

-10

-16

Salesforce and PrismHR perform aspects of computer processing for the cloud hosted Sequoia
People Platform. Data center facilities are ISO 27001:2013 certified and undergo periodic SOC 1 and
SOC 2 Type 2 report examinations. The servers hosted in Salesforce facilities are ISO 27001:2022
certified and undergo periodic SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 report examinations. Certification status and
the results of examinations are reviewed periodically as part of Sequoia’s monitoring controls and the
vendor management process.

User Entity Responsibilities

ne
ra.
i

o,

For user entities to derive the intended benefits of using the services of Sequoia, user entities have
certain additional responsibilities related to the system. These responsibilities are outlined below:
User entities are responsible for notifying Sequoia of service product issues, problems, or
incidents detected in their environments for resolution.

•

If user entities are using their own identity and authentication provider (SSO), user entities are
responsible for configuring application password settings in accordance with their own
policies and procedures as each system permits and also meets industry best practices.

•

User entities are responsible for proper use of the software and ensuring only authorized data
is uploaded to the system.

•

User entities are responsible for managing access to their account on the Sequoia People
Platform.

•

User entities should ensure that system users change login IDs and passwords from the initial
default values, if provided.

•

User entities should ensure that Sequoia is promptly notified of events that may prohibit the
complete, accurate, and timely completion of processing including, but not limited to,
problems with system functionality, performance/response, and telecommunications.

•

User entities should ensure that controls are in place to provide reasonable assurance that
client data sent by user entities is secured, complete, accurate, and timely.

•

User entities should develop their own disaster recovery and business continuity plans that
address the inability to access or utilize Sequoia services.

•

User entities should ensure that changes to authorized personnel are communicated to
Sequoia in a timely manner.

Section IV - Trust Services Categories, Criteria, Related Controls, Tests, and Test
Results
Tests of Operating Effectiveness
Armanino’s tests of the operating effectiveness of controls included tests that were considered
necessary to evaluate whether the controls were sufficient to provide reasonable, but not absolute,
assurance that the trust services criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria were satisfied throughout the
report period. In selecting our test procedures, we considered various factors including, but not limited
to, the following:
the nature of the control being tested and its frequency.

•

the types and completeness of available evidence.

•

the trust services criteria and HITRUST CSF criteria to be satisfied.

•

the degree to which the control relies on the effectiveness of other controls.

•

whether the control is manual or automated.

•

the expected efficiency and effectiveness of the test.

6.3
70
Z

0:5

Our tests of controls included observations, inspections, reperformance, and inquiries of appropriate
management, supervisory, and staff personnel seeking relevant information regarding the controls.
Additionally, the following table clarifies certain terms used in this section to describe the nature of
the tests performed.
Description

Inquiry

Inquiry of appropriate personnel and corroboration with management

Observation

Observation of the application, performance, or existence of the control

Inspection

Inspection of documents and reports indicating performance of the control

Reperformance

Reperformance of the control

requirements relating to such

determine whether the plan identified critical
business processes and integrated the
information security management requirements
of business continuity with other continuity
requirements relating to such aspects as
operations, staffing, materials, transport and
facilities.

06.d Data
Protection and
Privacy of
Covered
Information

The confidentiality and integrity
of covered and/or confidential
information at rest is protected
using an encryption method
appropriate to the medium
where it is stored; where the
organization chooses not to
encrypt covered and/or
confidential information, a
documented rationale for not
doing so is maintained or
alternative compensating
controls are used if the method
is approved and reviewed
annually by the CISO.

Inspected system configurations to determine
No exceptions
whether covered and/or confidential information noted
at rest was protected using an encryption method
appropriate to the medium where it was stored.
